name: Pearl Gross
life: “I still remember the click of my first hearing-aid case.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Pearl can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: My hearing aids flatten the bass. I held the counter and finally felt what people meant.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and a narrow brass watch set a little fast. Pearl has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with silvery hair gathered at the nape. Pearl draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Pearl can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To feel the bass from a safe seat.
family: Benedict Perreault is Pearl’s first cousin once removed. Pearl chooses an ordinary story to tell. Benedict asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The almost scholarship*, Benedict says, “I am the child's manager at the market. I'll hold one Saturday a month for as long as she wants it.”
connections: Adrian Trent. A seafarer's tune becomes something the neighbor can feel through the counter.

reactions.situation: The washer bearing goes quiet mid-song
reactions.response: Pearl listens for the missing note and lets maintenance know what changed.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Pearl offers to help correct the printed name and leaves it to the colleague whether any public explanation is wanted.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Pearl asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
